samples.summary: The `unescapeAll`-before-`validateLink` ordering is the plugin's entire scheme gate, and no test covers an encoded scheme (only the plain `javascript:` form)
samples.evidence: img-plugin.ts:128 resolves character references and backslash escapes (`md.utils.unescapeAll`) BEFORE the URL reaches `normalizeLink`/`validateLink` at lines 184-185. That ordering is what stops `` and `` — I traced both and they are blocked today: unescapeAll yields `javascript:alert(1)`, normalizeLink preserves the scheme, and markdown-it 14's `validateLink` (BAD_PROTO_RE `/^(vbscript|javascript|file|data):/`) refuses it. But the refused-list at img-plugin.test.ts:109 only exercises the *literal* `javascript:` spelling, and grep for `&#`/`entity`/`data:` in the test file returns nothing. A future refactor that moved `unescapeAll` after `validateLink` (or dropped it in favour of validating the raw attribute) would silently reopen an encoded-scheme bypass with the whole suite still green. Attacker action: any workspace member saves a note containing the encoded form; every collaborator's preview renders it. Add the encoded variants (and an allowed `data:image/png;base64,…` control) to the refused/accepted tables.

samples.summary: No test asserts that a `src` value carrying a `"` cannot break out of the emitted attribute, even though `parseAttrs` accepts such a value
samples.evidence: `` is ACCEPTED by parseAttrs: ATTR_RE's `'[^']*'` alternative (img-plugin.ts:83) captures `a" onerror="alert(1)` as the src, the junk checks at lines 107/131 see only whitespace, and the value reaches `state.push('image', ...)` at line 188. It is safe today only because two downstream layers both neutralise the quote — `normalizeLink` percent-encodes `"` to `%22` (mdurl's defaultChars excludes it) and markdown-it's `renderAttrs` runs `escapeHtml` (which covers `&<>"`) over every value. The plugin's stated premise ("markdown-it escapes the attribute values it emits", lines 37-39) is therefore load-bearing and unasserted: nothing in the suite would fail if a future change emitted the attribute string itself instead of a token, or set `token.attrSet` on a renderer path without escaping. Add a case asserting the rendered HTML contains no `onerror`/unescaped `"` for that input.

samples.summary: Author-controlled external `` with author-controlled dimensions is a reader-IP/User-Agent beacon; parity with `![]()` means no regression, but it widens a class this repo elsewhere refuses outright
samples.evidence: `validateLink` blocks only vbscript/javascript/file/non-image data URLs, so `` in a CRDT-shared note renders in every reader's session and hands the note's author each reader's IP, User-Agent and reading time. mermaid.ts:85-93 and docs/design/notes/notes.md:573-599 document this exact fetch-disclosure as the reason the mermaid path REFUSES `` and `img:` shape metadata, and both note that `the repo has no CSP today`. This is parity rather than a new hole — preview.test.ts:322 shows `![alt](https://example.com/img.png)` already renders an external image through the same `normalizeLink`/`validateLink` gate — so I am flagging it only because the new surface makes the zero-size (invisible) beacon trivially expressible via the `width`/`height` allowlist, and because the design doc added here does not repeat the disclosure caveat that the mermaid section makes explicit. The stated long-term fix (a restrictive `img-src` CSP) is still absent.
